*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK THE LIGHTHOUSE ACCORD ***

CHAPTER I

The keeper's cottage smelled of tar and old rope. Agnes set her case down on the
flagstones and waited for the man at the desk to acknowledge her.

"You're the replacement," Thomas said, not looking up from the logbook. "They
send me a girl from the mainland with soft hands and a certificate."

"They sent you a keeper," Agnes said. "The certificate is in the case. The hands
are my own business."

He looked up then. There was salt in his beard and something like amusement
behind the annoyance. "The last one lasted three weeks."

"The last one wasn't me."

"No," he admitted, closing the logbook. "Apparently not. Supper's at six. The
lamp is trimmed at dusk, whatever else is happening, whoever else is bleeding.
You'll learn the order of things."

"I already know the order of things," she said. "Lamp first. Everything else
after."

Thomas stood, and for the first time in eleven years, the stairs to the lantern
room did not feel entirely his own.

CHAPTER II

The storm came up from the southwest on the ninth day, the glass falling faster
than Thomas had ever seen it fall.

*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK THE LIGHTHOUSE ACCORD ***
